feature: Groups that arrange their own contents
summary: A group can now be a stack or a grid, so the things inside it space themselves instead of being nudged into place one at a time. Add a layer, delete one, or drag one past another and everything re-flows on its own, inside a component too.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. "Groups that arrange their own contents" is on by default.

try.do: On a blank canvas draw three rectangles roughly in a column, deliberately unevenly spaced.
Rubber-band all three and press ⌃⌘G (Layer ▸ Stack Selection). Nothing should move: the Gap it shows is read off the spacing you already had.
Type 8 into Gap and press Return.
Drag the second row up past the first. It should take first place rather than snapping back.
In the Layout section press Grid, then type 2 into Columns.
Press Stack again, press ⌥⌘K to make it a component, then drag a copy of it out of the Library.
Double-click into the original, select a row and press ⌘J to duplicate it.

evaluate: When you turned a hand-arranged group into a stack, did it feel like it read your spacing, or like it took it over?
Are Free / Stack / Grid the right three words, and is the top of the Layout section the right place for them?
Dragging a row past its neighbour reorders the stack. Did that read as helpful or as the app refusing your drag?
The row for the axis the stack decides says "Set by the stack" instead of a menu. Is that clear enough, or does it look broken?
Is one Gap number enough for a stack, or do you reach for padding on a plain group too?
rough: A stack is always exactly as big as its contents. There is no Hug / Fill / Fixed on the container yet, so you cannot say "this stack is 320 wide and the rows fill it" unless the container is a screen.
Padding is one number and only on a screen, because a plain group has no edges of its own. Per-side padding is not built.

Cut from the mock on purpose: the mock's Distribute row (packed / centre / between / around) means nothing in a container that is exactly as big as its contents, and its per-child Hug / Fill / Fixed would be a second control saying what the Horizontal and Vertical rows already say. The stack reuses those rows instead: the flow owns the axis it runs along, the placement rows own the other one.

The ui-grid mock's "layout grid" is a column overlay you eyeball against, not a container that positions what it holds. The ask was for a container, so that is what was built; the overlay is still unbuilt.
X and Y stop taking typing for a layer inside a stack, and say who owns them on hover. That is honest but it does mean the only way to move one row is to drag it, or to change the gap.
A locked layer inside a stack is still moved by the stack. Lock stops you dragging it; it does not opt out of the arrangement.
